resolvedOrPartiallyResolvedGaps.notes: Thirty-eight cases now exercise factual retrieval without full gold prose answers, subjective evaluation, network access, or canonical MoonCat fact changes. Coverage is 10 direct lookup, 10 cross-source synthesis, 10 provenance boundaries, and 8 live-verification stops; the Genesis, bounded on-chain synthesis, accessory-system, and naming evidence-boundary coverage gaps are covered.

The KB now records original-contract naming checks, CatNamed fields and zero-name semantics, raw/display/moderation boundaries, adjacent CatNamer provenance, and a deterministic 1,225-row historical/source-comparison snapshot. The reviewed CC0 MoonCatDAO name-index integration is the preferred revision-bounded source for finalized current names and canonical finalized history; provisional/live overlays remain excluded. Current storage, newer-than-reviewed state, current display counts, and live helper state remain explicit follow-up boundaries.
The 38-case factual benchmark covers contract-role/evidence synthesis; current state remains out of scope.

The KB now distinguishes 256 planned Genesis indices from the 96 released/adopted collection members and 160 permanently locked/unreleased indices. The exact released Cat ID/rescue-order mapping is cross-checked offline against existing bucket, trait-reference, and formula inputs. Vote outcome and participation are sourced while the technical lock mechanism remains unresolved; no current ownership, price, live state, or payment aggregate is imported.

The 12 Genesis rescue orders incorrectly present in Pink Panther were removed from the derived source and imported membership, reducing Pink Panther from 235 to 223. Canonical Genesis membership remains unchanged, character arrays are checked for duplicates and ascending order, and the validator now rejects any character-category overlap with canonical Genesis rescue orders.

All 18 decision files in the pinned MoonCatRescue dev-environment ADR directory are indexed with byte-checked source paths, status, source update date, and intent-versus-implementation limits. The snapshot does not claim current-master freshness, decision dates, authors, unspoken supersession, implementation completion, deployment, or live state.
Agents now have compact checked and manifest-derived API examples; examples still do not replace endpoint manifests or OpenAPI schemas.
Observed helper names and conservative input/output surfaces are indexed without importing source code or full mappings.

Previous empty hue/special/pale structures are replaced by ADR-aligned hue buckets, aggregate observed snapshot data, color source inventory, MoonCatColors internals summaries, and guardrails; per-cat mappings, exact RGB/hex palettes, full renderer behavior, BasePalette values, and mapColors override values remain out of scope.

A deterministic, source-backed policy now maps normal integer hues to ADR-shifted human-facing labels and handles Genesis black/white sentinels before circular hue handling. Raw hue fields remain untouched, pale remains a separate modifier, and palette/rendering claims remain out of scope.

Representative rescueOrder/catIdBytes5 round trips now cross-check LibMoonCat and mooncat_traits.json, Acclimated tokenId equivalence is verified only for the exact contract, and WMCR/accessory/palette/owned-record/batch/marketplace identifier conflations have explicit negative or unsupported fixtures.

Eight fixed fixtures retain bounded identity, trait, and parser-structure parity. The separate render artifact adds exact parser-derived palettes and X-major cells for all 25,440 IDs. MoonCatColors/on-chain palette parity, exact SVG serialization, accessories, live state, and licensing conclusions remain unavailable or excluded. Exhaustive checks cover every decoded row, full regeneration, parser equality and transpose-sensitive X/Y orientation.

Thirty-one realistic coding-agent cases now generate minimal route-backed packs with explicit warnings, forbidden claims, stop conditions, commands, and size metrics. The suite validates routing/context contracts and dangerous-conflation coverage without network or subjective model scoring.
Common agent workflows now have load order, outputs, guardrails, and stop conditions, and the recipe file is routed from data/agent-index.json.

Agents and developers now have wallet-free rescue-mining examples plus two dependency-free zero-network ESM conformance kits: a tagged static profile resolver over the existing population index and a supplied-log decoder over the existing contract/event registries. These examples add tested usage patterns without creating a second canonical dataset, fetching live state, scanning history, submitting transactions, or generalizing identifier meanings.
Rescue bucket status now records method/timestamp verification; identifier conversion and downstream-use boundaries still need caution.

data/ipfs-cids.json now records eight official MoonCatRescue source-observed CIDs/artifact folders and a supporting sourceRef; payload availability, file counts, schemas, and hash validation remain out of scope.
data/kb-gap-index.json is now directly discoverable from data/agent-index.json through the review-kb-gaps route.

The exact MoonCatsWrapped / Wrapped MoonCatsRescue contract is now verified at 0x7C40c393DC0f283F318791d746d894DdD3693572. Its WMCR token IDs are counter-allocated and mapping-backed to bytes5 cat IDs; the source contains no rescueOrder conversion. Other historical or unofficial wrappers remain outside this exact-contract review and must not inherit its behavior.

Color sources and claims are now inventoried separately from canonical color data, including ADR 0017, parser/source references, MoonCatColors surfaces, official guide context, MidnightLightning Reddit/Discord explanations, and observed trait snapshot context.

MoonCatColors internals now record compact verified semantics for colorsOf ordering, deriveColors ordering summary, accessoryColorsOf composition, paletteOf composition, mapColors purpose/application, hue helpers, and colorAlpha bands. Exact BasePalette values, mapColors keys/values, generated palettes, and per-cat outputs remain intentionally unimported.

The curated model decision now has a generated 25,440-row population index keyed by bytes5 catId with rescueOrder as a source-backed secondary lookup field, plus the retained 64-row fixture for lightweight tests. Names are pinned finalized enrichment; frequencies, live ownership/accessory state, markets, and provisional names remain outside the model.

A compact 28-file ChainStation source snapshot now pins master commit 5df03ab465d46f59f3e4d4a05e4e85fc90abdc0a and indexes ten application/data surfaces with exact evidence paths, source/configuration/runtime classifications, ADR-intent separation, benchmark coverage, and offline hash/shape validation. It intentionally excludes full-repository coverage, external responses, secrets, deployment verification, and live state.

Important active reference inputs now have local SHA-256/size checks, dependency mappings, copy/adaptation status, revision/date/license evidence, and explicit freshness limitations. The upstream commit/tag and retrieval date remain unresolved for core local reference files where checked-in evidence does not support a stronger claim.

The exact MoonCatAccessories contract now has a compact source-backed review of definitions, management, rescue-order assignment, OwnedAccessory storage, eligibility, metadata verification, Acclimated approvals, alteration/discontinuation, administration, identifier boundaries, and MoonCatAccessoryImages consumption. Full accessory data and current chain state remain unimported.

A deterministic 26-shard generated index now covers all 25,440 MoonCats with exhaustive identifier, LibMoonCat trait, parser, membership, color, naming, provenance, and hash validation plus local query/diff tooling. The unchanged 64-row sample remains a compact fixture. Live ownership, accessories, markets, provisional names, and freshness beyond pinned revisions remain excluded.
A zero-dependency read-only Python validator now checks data/*.json parsing, required routed file references, kb-gap sourceFiles, sourceRef consistency, and relatedFiles warnings.

Original browser rescue/mining behavior is now documented from the reviewed local mooncatrescue-web mirror files public/scan.html, public/js/mine.js, and public/js/mine-worker.js, cross-checked against data/protocol-constants.json. Wallet-free snippet and embeddable widget examples were added without importing frontend bundles, original image assets, Web3, workers, or transaction submission behavior; the widget now renders found catIds through the registered mooncatparser.js reference.

MoonCatSVGs internals record compact verified semantics for source identity, dependency interfaces, imageOf overload behavior, rescue-order conversion, default glow selection, SVG string assembly, output wrapper properties, and conceptual geometry/pattern surfaces. Its exact local ABI now routes through data/contract-registry.json; full Solidity source, coordinate constants, pattern arrays, generated SVG outputs, per-cat outputs, and accessory image composition remain intentionally unimported.

MoonCatAccessoryImages internals record compact verified semantics for source identity, rescue-order entrypoints, explicit versus lookup accessory lists, ownership preparation, foreground/background handling, glow branches, PNG data-URI assembly, and dependency boundaries. Its exact local ABI now routes through data/contract-registry.json; full Solidity source, accessory taxonomy, placement tables, palettes, IDAT data, PNG bytes, generated SVG or PNG outputs, per-cat outputs, and current accessory state remain intentionally unimported.

The thin integration overview connects definition management, rescue-order ownership, palette and zIndex alteration, verification filtering, PNG materialization, and SVG composition while keeping the two detailed reviews separate. Complete taxonomy, definitions, images, prices, supply, per-cat state, current availability, and exact generated output remain unresolved.

Exact address-bound ABI artifacts now cover all eight core materialization contracts plus adjacent WMCR; CatNamer remains semantic-only. All 32 extracted events retain exact signatures/order/indexing and Ethereum Keccak topic0, while five recipes preserve identifier, deployment/start, finality, naming, and current-state boundaries.

fileGaps.agentUsabilityImpact: Useful for locating selected MoonCat detail, filtering, API, wallet, rendering, Firebase, and build/deployment evidence without loading the full app; it must not be used as a live system report.
fileGaps.nextDataPass: Review an additional source area only through a separately scoped pinned snapshot, or run an explicitly authorized live verification for deployment/API/chain/gateway questions.

fileGaps.agentUsabilityImpact: Useful as a compact endpoint manifest, but agents should not treat it as full OpenAPI schema or verified runtime behavior for every response edge case.
fileGaps.nextDataPass: Re-sync from registered OpenAPI sources or live-check selected endpoints only in a focused API pass.
